questions.question: What is a cell?
questions.answer: A cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.

questions.question: Cells are the building blocks of all living organisms.
Which part of the cell controls all its activities?
Fill in the blank: The jelly-like substance inside the cell is called the ______.
What is the function of the cell membrane?
questions.answer: It controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.

questions.question: Observe the image and identify the cell shown.
Which image represents a plant cell?
Plant cells have a cell wall.
Fill in the blank: ______ are the green organelles where photosynthesis takes place.
Which organelle produces energy for the cell?
What is the function of the nucleus?
questions.answer: It controls the activities of the cell and contains genetic material.

questions.question: Animal cells do not have cell walls.
Observe the image and identify the highlighted organelle.
Which image shows chloroplasts?
Explain one difference between plant cells and animal cells.
questions.answer: Plant cells have a cell wall and chloroplasts, while animal cells do not.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The ______ is known as the powerhouse of the cell.
The cytoplasm contains the cell's organelles.
Which organelle is responsible for photosynthesis?
Why are cells called the basic unit of life?
questions.answer: Because all living organisms are made up of cells, and cells perform all life processes.

questions.question: Explain the functions of the cell membrane, nucleus, and cytoplasm.
questions.answer: The cell membrane controls movement of substances, the nucleus controls cell activities, and the cytoplasm contains organelles where many life processes occur.
